coldOpen: A truck fire shut Mont Blanc until 2002.
centralDependencyQuestion: How did one truck fire close a key Alpine tunnel for three years?

evidence.claim: On the morning of 24 March 1999, the engine of a Belgian transport truck carrying volatile freight caught fire in the tunnel.
The event expanded into a catastrophe which killed 39 people.
The fire led to a tunnel closure until 9 March 2002.
It reduces the route from France to Turin by 50 kilometres (30 miles) and to Milan by 100 km (60 mi).
The tunnel is 11.611 km (7.215 mi) in length, 8.6 m (28 ft) in width, and 4.35 m (14.3 ft) in height.
Within the tunnel, a minimum speed of 50 km/h and a maximum speed of 70 km/h applies, while the prescribed distance between vehicles is 150 m.
